hints: Look at the arrow directions in each diagram and separate the pairs acting in opposite directions from the pairs both acting upwards.
Recall that two equal opposite parallel forces form a couple whose torque is $F$ times the perpendicular separation and is the same about any point.
Compare the separation $d$ in diagram A with the separation $2d$ marked in the opposite-force diagram near the left side of the rod.
walkthrough: Identify the force directions: in A one $F$ is up and one $F$ is down, in B both are up, in C both are up, in D one $F$ is down and one $F$ is up.
A pure pivot-independent torque needs zero resultant force, so only the opposite-direction pairs in A and D are couples. B and C have resultant $2F$ upwards.
For a couple, torque magnitude is $\text{torque} = F \times \text{separation}$ between the lines of action.
In A the separation is $d$, so torque $= Fd$. In D the marked separation is $2d$, so torque $= F \times 2d = 2Fd$.
Since $2Fd > Fd$, and B and C do not give a pure couple torque, the largest torque is produced by the arrangement with opposite forces $2d$ apart. This is option D.

options.A: The forces are in opposite directions with separation $d$, so they form a couple of torque $F \times d = Fd$, which is not the largest.
options.B: Both forces act upwards in the same direction, so there is a resultant force $2F$ and no pure couple, with zero net moment about the centre of the $5d$ rod.
options.C: Both forces act upwards in the same direction separated by $2d$, so they do not form a couple and do not give a pivot-independent torque.
options.D: The forces are in opposite directions with separation $2d$, so they form a couple of torque $F \times 2d = 2Fd$, the largest pure torque.
